ruleName: Ball Moved by Natural Forces / Ball Stopped by Player’s Equipment
imagePrompt: Create a polished, modern, semi-realistic (about 75% realistic, 25% stylised) illustration in the established junior golf quiz style. Show a scene on a short grass fairway with a gentle slope. A golf ball has come to rest against a golf club lying flat on the ground, used to measure a relief area. The player is present but not touching the club or ball and appears to be observing the situation. Do not include text, labels, numbers, arrows, captions, diagrams, badges, logos, watermarks, club crests, scorecards or speech bubbles. Focus on clearly displaying the ball against the club and the measurement scenario.
imageAlt: A golf ball at rest up against a club on a fairway slope, with a player standing nearby and not interfering.

sceneSpec.setting: On the fairway, slightly sloping ground with short grass.
sceneSpec.players: One player present, not interacting with the ball or club at the moment shown.
sceneSpec.ballPosition: Golf ball at rest, touching and up against a club that is lying on the ground.
sceneSpec.ruleMoment: The precise moment after the ball, moved by the wind, has rolled and come to rest against the club placed as a measuring aid.
sceneSpec.educationalFocus: Understanding what happens when a ball moved by natural forces is stopped by equipment set down for measuring.
mustShow: A golf ball at rest in contact with a club lying flat on the fairway to measure a relief area.
The ball's original lie and the resting position against the club.
mustNotShow: Text, labels, numbers, arrows, captions, diagrams, badges, logos, watermarks, club crests, scorecards or speech bubbles.
Any element suggesting the ball is being deliberately touched or stopped by the player.

questions.title: Ball Blown by Wind and Stopped by Your Club on the Ground
questions.question: You put your club on the ground to see how far you can drop your ball. Before you do anything else, the wind blows your ball and it rolls until it hits your club and stops. What should you do?

choices.text: No penalty. Play the ball from where it stopped by the club.
No penalty. Move your club and put the ball back where it was before it moved.
One-shot penalty because your club stopped the ball.
You must drop the ball again.

questions.explanation: Your club on the ground stopped your ball after the wind moved it. There is no penalty, but you must move your club and put the ball back where it was before.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: The area where you are allowed to drop your ball.
Put the ball back where it was before it moved.

questions.teachingTip: Show children how to carefully put the ball back where it started if it is moved by wind and stopped by something you placed on the ground.
likelyMisconceptions: Children might think they should play from where the ball stopped.
They might think there is a penalty because the club stopped the ball.

questions.title: Ball Moved by Wind and Stopped by Measuring Club
questions.question: You place a club on the ground to measure a relief area. Before you continue, your ball is moved by wind and rolls until it comes to rest against the club you laid on the ground. What is the correct ruling?

choices.text: No penalty. Play the ball from where it now lies against the club.
No penalty. Move the club and replace the ball on its original spot.
One-stroke penalty for stopping the ball with your equipment.
You must drop the ball again.

questions.explanation: Although the wind caused the ball to move, your club deliberately placed on the ground stopped the ball from continuing to move. The ball must be replaced on its original spot with no penalty.
